description: Out-of-game asset manager for EVE Online: assets, wealth tracking, market orders, transactions, industry jobs and stockpiles across characters and corporations.
notes: jEveAssets needs Java 8 or newer, 64-bit, with javaw on the PATH.
With Scoop: scoop bucket add java; scoop install java/temurin-jre
Accounts, profiles and history live in %USERPROFILE%\.jeveassets, outside the Scoop folder:
they survive updates and are kept on uninstall.
Package manager mode is on, so jEveAssets does not update itself; use 'scoop update jEveAssets'.
Static data (items, locations) comes with each release; upstream also publishes data-only updates
between releases, and those reach you with the next release.
The shortcut starts jmemory.jar, which runs jEveAssets with the heap size from jmemory.properties
(xmx=1g by default). The file is persisted: edit it there to give jEveAssets more memory.
When adding an account, choose the localhost login: the other option sends the login code
On the first start Windows Firewall may ask about Java: jEveAssets opens port 2222 on all
interfaces only to detect a second copy of itself. Blocking it is safe.
pre_install: # jEveAssets answers on 127.0.0.1:2222 while it runs (its single-instance check). It runs in javaw.exe
# from the Java folder, which Scoop's own 'is it running' check does not see.
if ($running) { error "$app seems to be running (something answers on 127.0.0.1:2222). Close it and try again."; break }
# Package manager mode: no self-update and no update prompts; Scoop delivers new versions.
# Heap size for jmemory.jar. Created only once; after that the persisted copy is used.
# The jar runs through javaw, so no console window stays open.
# The icon exists only as PNGs inside the jar; build the .ico for the shortcut from them.
if (!(Test-Path -LiteralPath $iconTool)) { error "Cannot build the icon: '$iconTool' is missing."; break }
pre_uninstall: # 'scoop update' and 'scoop uninstall' stop here, before anything is removed, while jEveAssets runs.
if ($running) { error "$app seems to be running (something answers on 127.0.0.1:2222). Close it and try again."; break }
